methodology: Every insight cites the specific ratio/period pair it is derived from in ratios_timeseries.json.

risk_signals.statement: NPL ratio nearly doubled from 4.62% (FY2014) to 8.01% (FY2016), the highest point in the 13-year series, then steadily improved for three straight years to 3.63% (FY2019) — a multi-year shock that fully resolved rather than compounding.

UPDATED (was 'warning', capped at FY2023 — now materially worse): NPL ratio rose from 2.55% (FY2020) to 5.99% (FY2022), 5.50% (FY2023), 14.90% (FY2024) and 15.50% (FY2025), while CAR declined every year since FY2020's peak of 14.92% to 12.58% (FY2023), 10.59% (FY2024) and 8.42% (FY2025). CAR is NO LONGER above the regulatory minimum: it breached the 12.50% (with-buffer) requirement in FY2024 and the reported capital shortfall nearly tripled from BDT (9,728.77)m (FY2024) to BDT (26,596.35)m (FY2025). Asset quality and capital adequacy have now moved in the wrong direction simultaneously for five consecutive years.

UPDATED (FY2023's 6.41% is no longer the series low): ROE fell further to 1.44% in FY2024 and 1.52% in FY2025, both far below the FY2023 figure that was itself already a series low at the time and well below the FY2011-2015 average (~17%). The FY2024 collapse was driven by a near-tripling of provisioning (Total Provision excl. tax: BDT 4,548m FY2023 -> BDT 12,933m FY2024, derivable as operating_profit minus profit_before_tax in each year's quarterly file) as NPL recognition accelerated; FY2025's continued near-zero ROE (net profit after tax of just BDT 635.8m on total assets of BDT 884,056.45m) occurred despite -- and is arguably flattered by -- a forborne BDT 55,949.30m provision shortfall described in the qualified_audit_opinion signal below.

FY2024 was UCB's own version of the sector-wide asset-quality recognition event described across this dataset's other banks: NPL ratio nearly tripled from 5.50% (FY2023) to 14.90% (FY2024, classified loans BDT 27,819m -> BDT 85,344m), and CAR breached the regulatory minimum for the first time in this 15-year series (10.59% vs a required-with-buffer BDT 63,587.78m against actual Total Capital of BDT 53,859m, a reported Capital Surplus/(Shortage) of BDT (9,728.77)m). Even though absolute specific provisions rose (BDT 13,907m -> BDT 22,341m), coverage of the much larger NPL base fell from 49.99% to 26.18% -- provisioning did not keep pace with newly recognized bad loans, and net profit after tax collapsed 77% (BDT 2,685m -> BDT 608m).

UCB PLC's FY2025 audited financial statements (signed 30 April 2026 by Aziz Halim Khair Choudhury, PKF Global network) carry a QUALIFIED opinion. Basis: required loan-loss provision of BDT 76,794.22m vs. BDT 25,243.80m actually maintained (a shortfall of BDT 51,550.40m), plus a further other-assets shortfall of BDT 4,398.90m (including an unrecognized BDT 4,380.20m impairment on 99.99%-owned subsidiary UCB Fintech Company Ltd / 'Upay', which itself has cumulative losses of BDT 4,380.20m) -- combined BDT 55,949.30m, which Bangladesh Bank explicitly permitted the bank not to recognize when finalizing FY2025 accounts (forbearance letter BSD-5(Wing-3)/104/2026-410, 29 April 2026). The auditor states in its own report that absent this forbearance, UCB 'would have incurred an aggregate loss of BDT 32,788.80m' (vs. the BDT 635.80m profit actually reported -- a swing of roughly BDT 334bn) 'and the CRAR would have declined to 0.93%' (vs. the reported 8.42%, which is itself already below the 12.50% regulatory minimum). This is a materially larger and more explicit recognition-vs-deferral gap than FY2024's, and is disclosed by the auditor rather than inferred from ratios, unlike this dataset's other flagged banks.

Specific-provision coverage of classified loans fell for three straight years -- 49.99% (FY2023) -> 26.18% (FY2024) -> 20.13% (FY2025) -- even as classified loans grew every year (BDT 27,819m -> BDT 85,344m -> BDT 95,762.32m) and the NPL ratio rose every year (5.50% -> 14.90% -> 15.50%). Reported net profit after tax alone (BDT 2,685m -> BDT 608m -> BDT 635.80m) understates the deterioration: it appears to stabilize in FY2025 only because of the forborne provision shortfall described in the qualified_audit_opinion signal above, not because underlying asset quality improved.

Newly-added quarterly data (2026-08-26 session) reveals UCB posted a net loss of BDT -999.76m in Q1-2013 (Jan-Mar, cumulative) alone -- invisible in the annual figures, since FY2013 as a whole was a solid BDT 3,065.41m profit. The loss fully reversed by Q2-2013 (cumulative net profit turned positive at BDT 1,058.69m), then continued rising through Q3 (BDT 1,527.56m) to the full-year BDT 3,065.41m. This is the only quarter-level loss found anywhere in the newly-added 2013-2016 quarterly data (every other quarter from Q1-2014 through Q3-2016 was cumulative-profitable), and is a concrete example of the within-year volatility that year-end-only reporting conceals -- exactly the gap this project's Q1-Q3 backfill effort exists to close.

Newly-added quarterly data (2026-08-27 session, now covering Q1-Q3 2017-2025) shows UCB's Q1-2017 cumulative net profit after tax collapsed to just BDT 19.92m (EPS 0.02) -- a near-zero trough sitting right at the tail of the FY2016 NPL-spike period already flagged in the '2016_npl_spike_recovered' signal above (NPL 8.01% at FY2016-end, the series high before its multi-year recovery). Profitability then recovered quarter by quarter through the rest of 2017 (Q2 cumulative BDT 1,156.52m, Q3 cumulative BDT 2,387.49m) and continued a broad multi-year recovery through 2018-2019, consistent with -- and adding quarterly granularity to -- the already-documented FY2016-to-FY2019 NPL-ratio recovery.

The newly-added 2024_Q3.json cumulative figures, combined with the already-recorded FY2024 annual figures, reveal that Q4-2024 ALONE (Oct-Dec, i.e. FY2024 annual minus the 9-month cumulative) was a net loss of approximately BDT -2,009.12m -- calculated as FY2024 profit_after_tax (BDT 608m, from 2024_Q4.json) minus the 9-month cumulative net_profit_after_tax_cumulative (BDT 2,617.12m, from 2024_Q3.json). This was NOT an operating-performance collapse: Q4-alone operating profit (profit before provision) was still a healthy +BDT 2,007.65m (FY2024's BDT 15,078m minus the 9-month BDT 13,070.35m), essentially in line with the rest of the year. The swing to a net loss was driven entirely by a sudden concentration of provisioning in the final quarter -- consistent with, and adding precise quarterly timing to, the already-documented 'fy2024_sector_wide_recognition_event' signal above (NPL 5.50%->14.90%, Total Provision excl. tax BDT 4,548m FY2023 -> BDT 12,933m FY2024): most of that provisioning increase landed in Q4 specifically, turning a profitable first nine months into a loss-making year-end close. This is a clean example of exactly the kind of within-year volatility this project's quarterly backfill effort exists to surface, on the same pattern as the already-documented Q1-2013 loss.

A genuine, unexplained restatement was found while cross-validating the newly-added 2017-2025 quarterly data: UCB's own Q3-2019 interim filing reports net_profit_after_tax_cumulative (Jan-Sep 2019, Bank) of BDT 1,885.99m, but the Q3-2020 interim filing's own comparative column for the identical period instead shows BDT 1,816.79m -- a ~3.7% / BDT 69.2m gap with no stated reason in either filing. Per this project's standing convention, the contemporaneous 2019 figure (1,885.99m) is the one recorded in 2019_Q3.json; the later, lower figure is not applied. This is the same kind of silent comparative-column drift already documented for FY2015/FY2016 and FY2023 NAV-per-share elsewhere in this file, now also observed in a quarterly net-profit figure.

historical_context: UCB shows a long-run profitability decline (ROE from 24.77% in FY2011 to a low-single-digit range from FY2023 onward: 6.41% FY2023, 1.44% FY2024, 1.52% FY2025) alongside two distinct NPL cycles: a FY2016 spike that fully resolved by FY2019, and a renewed climb from FY2020 that accelerated sharply into a sector-wide recognition event in FY2024 (NPL 5.50%->14.90%) and continued deteriorating in FY2025 (NPL 14.90%->15.50%). Capital adequacy breached the regulatory minimum in FY2024 and the shortfall nearly tripled in FY2025 (Capital Surplus/(Shortage) BDT (9,728.77)m -> BDT (26,596.35)m). Newly-added Q1-Q3 2024 data shows this was heavily back-loaded: UCB was solidly profitable through the first nine months of 2024 (cumulative net profit BDT 2,617.12m at Q3) before a concentrated wave of Q4 provisioning turned the full year into just BDT 608m -- meaning Q4-2024 alone was a roughly BDT 2.0 billion net loss. FY2025's audited financial statements carry a QUALIFIED audit opinion: a Bangladesh-Bank-forborne provision shortfall of BDT 55,949.30m that the auditor states would otherwise have produced a BDT 32,788.80m loss and a 0.93% CRAR instead of the reported BDT 635.80m profit and 8.42% CRAR. This combination -- deteriorating asset quality, a widening capital shortfall, and now an explicit audit qualification quantifying just how much reported profitability depends on regulatory forbearance rather than economic reality -- makes UCB one of the more severe cases in this dataset as of FY2025, comparable in kind to (and by some measures worse than) the NBL/IFIC/ABBANK/ISLAMIBANK patterns already documented for FY2024 across other banks in this project.
data_gaps: Q4/year-end (audited) data is available for FY2011-2025. Q1/Q2/Q3 (cumulative from 1 Jan) is now available for FY2013 through FY2025 -- FY2013-2016 sourced from each annual report's own embedded 'Evaluation of Quarterly Financial Statements' audit-committee disclosure table (added in the 2026-08-26 session), and FY2017-2025 (all 27 possible quarters, added in the 2026-08-27 session) sourced instead from UCB's own genuine standalone unaudited interim financial statements on ucb.com.bd's investor-relations archive, since UCB discontinued the embedded annual-report table after FY2016 (re-confirmed this session). See sources.json for full extraction detail on both eras, including: the FY2015/FY2016 annual-report PDFs being pure image scans requiring re-OCR (2026-08-26 session); most FY2017-2023 and FY2025-Q1/Q2 interim-statement PDFs also being pure image scans requiring a full OCR pipeline, and the FY2024/FY2025-Q3 interim PDFs instead having a corrupted embedded-font character mapping requiring targeted re-render-and-OCR (2026-08-27 session); and one genuine net-profit restatement found between the Q3-2019 and Q3-2020 filings (see the 2019_q3_profit_restatement_discrepancy risk signal above). FY2011-2012 genuinely have no embedded annual-report table (confirmed by inspecting both years' full table of contents; the table did not exist before BSEC's August-2012 Corporate Governance Notification) -- but the SAME ucb.com.bd interim-statements archive used for 2017-2025 also lists real standalone filings for 2011-2012, so a full FY2011-2012 is very likely still recoverable. This was only partially completed in the 2026-08-27 session: 2011 Q1 was found, downloaded, extracted, cross-checked and written up (quarterly/2011_Q1.json) from a clean native-text PDF; 2011 Q2 (Half-Yearly) and Q3, and all of 2012 (Q1, Half-Yearly, Q3), remain downloaded-and-confirmed-to-exist but not yet extracted -- 2011 Q3's own PDF is an unusually dense single-page 3-column layout (Consolidated and Solo statements crammed together) that defeated straightforward text-linearization (though a partial manual read did confirm Solo Total Assets of BDT 152,535.63m for 30-Sep-2011, consistent with steady growth from Q1's BDT 136,561.72m), and 2012's filings are pure image scans needing the same OCR pipeline used for 2017-2023. This is flagged as the natural next slice of work rather than a dead end. FY2025 Q4 is a partial exception to 'audited': the underlying financial statements are audited (with a qualified opinion), but no FY2025 Annual Report (the bank's usual five-year-summary format) could be retrieved -- uds.ucb.com.bd (where the bank's own website links its FY2025 annual report) refused all connections, the equivalent main-domain URL is a 1-page placeholder, and Wayback Machine has no capture of either. FY2025 figures were instead OCR'd from a scanned audited financial-statements PDF (see sources.json for the multi-way cross-validation performed) and market_price_per_share/nav_per_share/eps for FY2025 come from supplementary sources (this project's own DSE price archive and UCB's Price-Sensitive-Information notice) rather than the primary filing itself. ldr_pct for FY2025 Q4 (and, by the same convention, for every newly-added FY2017-2025 Q1/Q2/Q3 quarter) is a simple Gross-Loans/Deposits calculation and is NOT directly comparable to the bank's own historically-reported regulatory Credit-deposit ratio used in FY2011-2024's own annual reports (see each period's own period_note / ratios_timeseries.json basis field). A minor unresolved discrepancy: FY2023 NAV/share is 29.68 in FY2023's own report vs. 28.30 restated in FY2024's comparative column (kept as 29.68 per project convention; see sources.json). A second, similar discrepancy was found in the 2026-08-26 session for FY2015: NAV/share is 25.49 in FY2015's own report vs. 30.59 in FY2016's comparative column, the latter appearing to be a genuine computation error (see the 2013-2016 Q1/Q2/Q3 source entry in sources.json). ROA/ROE and NPL ratio / provision coverage / CAR are null for every Q1/Q2/Q3 period across the whole 2013-2025 span, since none of UCB's interim (unaudited) filings of either era disclose asset-quality or capital-adequacy figures, and this project has not yet settled on an annualization convention for a cumulative sub-annual ROA/ROE.
